title: S2A grid/layout contract defs (curation)
description: The judgment layer of a grid contract. Evidence can read what the CSS and the Figma grid modes say; it cannot say which container family is canonical, which tier owns a rule, or what should happen at a boundary. Those live here, are written by people, and are reviewed in PRs. out/<slug>.contract.json is generated from defs + evidence and must never be hand-edited.

version.description: Semver for the generated contract. Omitted means 0.1.0.

kind.description: foundation: the shared vocabulary (breakpoints, columns, gutters). container: a width/margin family. grid: a placement system children opt into. spacing: the vertical rhythm between sections.

tier.description: Who owns the rule. Will Blanton's framing: global and sectional belong to S2A, block-level belongs to C2. A block-tier contract is documented here but must not add shipped tokens to S2A.

status.description: shipped: implemented in packages/grid and verified. proposed: specified in Figma or in Will's layout page with no S2A implementation yet; rules assert absence so the gate stays honest. deprecated: superseded, kept so consumers can migrate.

supersededBy.description: Slug of the contract that replaces this one. Required when status is deprecated.

stylesheet.description: Repo-relative path to the stylesheet of record.

rootClass.description: The class a consumer puts on the element. Null for a foundation contract that defines no class of its own.

childClass.description: The class the children of rootClass carry, when the system has one.

nodeId.description: The frame or section of record on Will's layout page.

collectionId.description: Variable collection the values come from, e.g. VariableCollectionId:6:178.

layerName.description: The layer-name convention this contract corresponds to, e.g. 'Column flex-Grid-8'.

designOnly.description: True when the Figma variables behind this contract are design-only by intent (underscore-prefixed, stripped by build-tokens.js). Design-only means the values are evidence to check code against, never a source for shipped CSS.

breakpointBehavior.description: What this contract does in each breakpoint range. One entry per breakpoint id the foundation defines.

maxWidth.description: Resolved max width, a token ref in {s2a.…} form, or null for unconstrained.

margin.description: Token ref or percentage rule for the side margins.

breakpoints.description: Foundation contracts only: the canonical ranges. Every other contract references these by id.

figmaMode.description: Mode name in the Figma responsive collection.

figmaLabel.description: The _breakpoint label Will set on the mode, e.g. 'Desktop XL'.

minWidth.description: Null for the mobile-first base range, which carries no media query.

mockWidth.description: The static mockup width designers draw at in this range.

portraitEscape.description: The agreed portrait-reflow breakpoint inside this range, when one exists.

tokens.description: Every token this contract binds, by role. Refs use {s2a.…} dotted form (Figma variable names with slashes as dots).

role.description: What the token does here: gutter, margin, max-width, row-height, section-gap.

surface.description: The code surface a consumer touches. Validated against the extracted code evidence.

pattern.description: For a family, the shape of the name, e.g. 'col-{bp}-{1..12}'.

rules.description: Machine-checkable assertions. This is the whole point: a layout rule nobody can check is a convention, not a contract. Each rule names a check type the validator implements.

statement.description: The rule in plain language, as a designer or dev would read it.

type.description: mediaQueryPresent: the grid stylesheet declares a range starting at minWidth. boundaryAgreement: the grid stylesheet and the shipped responsive token file agree on where a breakpoint begins. classPresent/classAbsent: the class exists (or deliberately does not yet). customPropertyEquals: a --s2a-grid-* property resolves to a px value in a given range. declarationEquals: a declaration on a class resolves, through var() chains, to a px value. tokenShipped: the token reference exists in the built token CSS. figmaAgrees: the Figma grid mode holds the value this contract claims, so a change in the design file surfaces here. manual: a rule a person must confirm; recorded so it is visible, never counted as passing.

decisions.description: The questions evidence cannot answer. An open decision is not a blocker; it is the thing the contract is honest about.

visualize.description: How Storybook should render this contract. The story reads the generated contract, so a visualization cannot drift from the rules it illustrates.

spans.description: Example span rows to render, e.g. [[6,6],[8,4],[4,4,4]].

overlay.description: Whether the column overlay applies to this demo.
